subject: FrostEdge renewal: request for price stability and credit structure
messages:
From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@frostedge.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, procurement@frostedge.com
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — stability request for upcoming term

Hi Vanessa,

We're starting our vendor budgeting cycle and want to lock the renewal for FrostEdge's Redwood plan (current seat/commit) by mid-May. Recent traffic growth means we'll exceed our committed tokens in Q3, but the board is asking for a temporary price stability window while we finalize forecast adjustments.

Key asks from our side:
- A 6–9 month price hold at current blended rate (or smaller step-down)
- One-time usage credits to offset Q3 burst overage while we migrate some workloads to staging
- Confirmation that peak capacity (burst) will be available during onboarding windows

Can we get a commercial response and a redline we can take to procurement? Maya from procurement (cc'd) will lead the PO. Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Oliver
Oliver Grant
Head of Platform
FrostEdge

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@frostedge.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@frostedge.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — stability request for upcoming term

Hi Oliver — thanks for the transparency and the timeline. We value FrostEdge as a long-term partner and want to avoid disrupting your launch cadence.

I've attached a short counter (FrostEdge_Renewal_Counter_v1.pdf) that tries to balance predictability and operational cost:
- 6-month price hold at current blended rate from renewal effective date
- One-time credit equal to 10% of projected Q3 overage (applied as invoice credit)
- Commitment to guaranteed burst capacity for two scheduled onboarding windows (up to X GPUs)

A few things we'd need from procurement to finalize quickly:
1) Confirmation of expected committed token increase (or a target range) so we can size pool/quotas
2) A signed amendment or PO by 15 May to lock the pricing

Ben and Grace are looped for approval on the credit and burst carve-outs — Ben, can you confirm the finance guardrails on a 10% overage credit? Grace, can ops commit to the two-window burst reservation?

If it's easier, we can do a 20-minute call tomorrow to walk it through.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: FrostEdge_Renewal_Counter_v1.pdf (1 page — commercial terms)

From: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@frostedge.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@frostedge.com>, procurement@frostedge.com
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 14:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — stability request for upcoming term

Vanessa, thanks for the quick turn. A few clarifying items from procurement and engineering:

- The business is pushing for a 9-month hold rather than 6, to carry through Q4 budget revisions. Is there flexibility to stretch to 9 months with a small step after month 6?
- For credits: procurement prefers fixed credits expressed as USD (easier for POs). Can Redwood convert the 10% projected overage to a not-to-exceed USD credit amount?
- Ops question: the team needs assurance that burst reservations won't be preempted by higher-priority tenants — can you confirm isolation guarantees for the two windows?

I'm attaching our usage export for Mar-Apr to help size the commit delta (FrostEdge_Monthly_Usage_Report_Mar-Apr_2027.csv). If you can provide a short write-up with the final USD credit number and the 9-month vs 6-month tradeoffs, procurement can finish the PO.

Oliver

Attachment: FrostEdge_Monthly_Usage_Report_Mar-Apr_2027.csv

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@frostedge.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@frostedge.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 16:38:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: FrostEdge renewal — next steps and internal approval request

Ben / Grace — forwarding the latest from FrostEdge. Summary and next steps:

Summary of asks from FrostEdge:
- Prefer 9-month price hold (vs our proposed 6); budget team wants runway through Q4
- Wants a USD-denominated one-time credit (procurement prefers this for PO clarity)
- Needs guarantee that two onboarding windows will have reserved burst capacity without preemption

Our proposed commercial counter (from the attached PDF):
- Maintain 6-month hold at current blended rate; offer an optional extension to 9 months if FrostEdge increases committed tokens by >= 25% at signing (this reduces risk on our side)
- Convert the 10% projected overage credit into a capped USD credit: we calculated $45,000 not-to-exceed credit based on the usage file they sent (outline in the attached PDF)
- Ops to reserve burst capacity for two 48-hour windows; provide SLA carve-out language to avoid preemption during those windows

Approvals needed:
- Ben: sign-off on the $45k capped credit and final wording on invoice-credit vs. prepaid credit
- Grace: confirm the operational isolation guarantee and provide the exact reservation process (how we schedule and who owns the ticket)

If we get Ben+Grace sign-off today, I'll send back the revised PDF with the USD credit and the 9-month contingency language, and ask procurement to share a PO template. If we can't extend to 9 months without a commit increase, propose we offer a phased extension: 6 months guaranteed + optional 3-month hold (at a 2.5% step-up) exercisable by FrostEdge within the first 30 days.

Please reply with short approvals or redlines. Oliver / Maya — you'll see the final doc as soon as we have internal OK.

Thanks,
Vanessa

--
